text.p: Following are the main stories from Austrian newspapers on Wednesday.
- Job crisis despite high season. Structural problems in the tourism industry having a big impact on job market. Economists say over 200,000 will be looking for work this summer.
- Road pricing does little damage to business. Transport costs have only risen marginally, experts say.
- Prices up at the petrol pump. Oil multinationals and traders do not rule out further fuel price increases as spot prices rise in Rotterdam and some refineries have technical problems.
- Sanitised Raiffeisen giant AMF is to be sold. Planned stock exchange listing could bring in one billion schillings. Also negotiations with three interested parties.

- Road pricing for heavy goods vehicles and buses alone will bring the government no money, according to the Chamber of Economy. Costs of setting up the system have to be deducted from an estimated annual revenue of 3.4 billion schillings.
- Ping-pong game in pensions. Social Affairs Minister Lore Hostasch is demanding the social partners (employers and unions) show more willingness to compromise in reform talks.
- Amost 200,000 without a job this summer. Labour market crisis in building and tourism. Unemployment is rising dramatically. The number of employed is also near a record high.
- Bank Austria group: good earnings must be lasting. Bank Austria and Creditanstalt: share exchange ratio should be fixed by end of August.
- The paper industry wants more flexibility. Employers expect no pay rises in this round. Unions want a package to include shorter working times.

- Pension reform is creating a billion-schilling hole. According to the Chamber of Economy reform will bring the government more money in the short term but cost far more than it brings in the medium term.
- Gasoline prices are at a record high in Austria. The firm dollar could lead to further price increases.
- Number of overnight stays in Austria down 2.7 million. Guests are running away. Experts say the whole industry is out of kilter in terms of prices and product offer.
